title: Dynamic Programming

views.title: Linear DP & State Machines
views.intro: Run the six-step framework on every problem: state, choice, transition, base, order, shrink. One climbing-stairs problem is written three ways (memo, table, O(1)) so you can move between them on demand.
table: Count ways or min cost where step i reads a few earlier steps
Best subarray ending here (track max and min for products)
Holding / not holding, transactions used, cooldown, fee

files.desc: Climbing stairs x3, rob, decode ways, Kadane, max product, stock I-IV + cooldown + fee

pitfalls: Max product needs both max AND min: a negative flips them.
Decode ways: a leading zero kills the one-digit option; 10 and 20 are the only valid two-digit zeros.
Stock with k transactions: if k >= n/2 it degenerates to unlimited.

views.title: Knapsack Family
views.intro: Loop direction over capacity decides reuse: downward means each item once, upward means reusable. For counting, coins outer gives combinations; amount outer gives ordered sequences.
table: Subset under a capacity, each item once
Split count into 1,2,4,... chunks then run 0/1
Partition, target sum, last stone II

files.desc: 0/1, unbounded, bounded, subset sum, partition, target sum, coin change min/ways, combination sum IV, perfect squares, ones and zeroes

pitfalls: Iterating capacity upward in a 0/1 problem silently reuses items.
Coin Change II (combinations) vs Combination Sum IV (sequences) differ only in loop order.
Target Sum: the reduction is subsets summing to (total + target) / 2; check parity and range first.

views.title: Sequences & Strings
views.intro: Two sequences give a prefix table dp[i][j]. One sequence with a pairwise condition gives LIS-style dp or the O(n log n) tails array. Palindromes use interval dp or center expansion.
table: Longest chain, each element larger than the previous
Two strings, match or edit prefixes
Interval dp or expand around a center

files.desc: LIS (both forms), count of LIS, envelopes, LCS, edit distance, palindromes, distinct subsequences, word break, wildcard, regex, interleave

pitfalls: Russian Doll: sort width ascending and height DESCENDING so equal widths cannot chain.
Subsequence means order kept, substring means contiguous: contiguous resets to 0 on mismatch.
Regex star: zero copies is dp[i][j-2]; one more copy needs the preceding char to match.

views.title: Grid & Interval DP
views.intro: Grids depend on up/left (or backward for dungeon-style). Interval dp answers a range [i, j] by trying every split k; loop by length. In burst balloons, k is the LAST item processed.
table: Right/down moves, count or min/max path sum
Min of three neighbors plus one
Matrix chain, burst balloons, cut stick, strange printer
Score difference the mover can force

files.desc: Unique paths, min path sum, triangle, maximal square, dungeon, cherry pickup II, burst balloons, matrix chain, cut stick, palindrome cuts, strange printer, stone game

pitfalls: Dungeon must run backward: the minimum health needed depends on what comes AFTER.
Burst balloons: think "last to burst" so the two sides become independent.
Pad the array with sentinels (1 at both ends) instead of special-casing borders.

views.title: Bitmask & Digit DP
views.intro: Bitmask dp when n <= 20 and you must use each item once: dp[mask]. Digit dp when counting numbers up to N with a digit property: state is (position, tight, started, property).
table: Each worker takes one task, position = popcount(mask)
Fill buckets, track sum mod target
Memoize on the set of numbers taken
Count x in [0, N] with a property

files.desc: Assignment, k equal subsets, beautiful arrangement, can I win, digit one count, digit set, repeated digits

pitfalls: Digit dp: `tight` is only true while every prefix digit equals the bound; `started` handles leading zeros.
Subset enumeration `sub = (sub - 1) & mask` totals 3^n across all masks.
Use Integer.bitCount(mask) as the implicit "how many placed" index.

views.title: DP + Other Structures
views.intro: The hard-round combinations: dp with binary search (job scheduling), dp with a monotonic deque (jump game VI), probability dp, hash-map state, and memoized DFS on an implicit DAG.
table: Weighted job scheduling: best profit up to the last compatible job
Window max over earlier dp values
Distribution over states after k steps
Longest increasing path in a grid

files.desc: Job scheduling, constrained subset sum, jump game VI, knight probability, new 21 game, arithmetic subsequence, longest increasing path

pitfalls: When transitions look at a sliding window of earlier dp values, reach for a monotonic deque before a segment tree.
Longest increasing path needs no visited set: strictly increasing values make the graph a DAG.

views.title: DP: Hard Variants
views.intro: Hard DP adds an extra dimension to a known shape: attached count (remove boxes), pile count (merge stones), two walkers (cherry pickup), difference as state (tallest billboard), or flipping the question (egg drop).
table: Remove boxes, merge stones, palindromic subsequences
Egg drop: floors per move count

files.desc: Frog jump, stone game II, predict the winner, super egg drop, dice rolls to target, paint house II, cherry pickup, out of boundary paths, domino tiling, distinct palindromic subsequences, profitable schemes, tallest billboard, best team score, remove boxes, merge stones, min cost tree from leaf values, shortest common supersequence, minimum insertions, three non-overlapping subarrays, delete and earn, integer break, divisible subset, string chain, vowel permutations, attendance record

pitfalls: State the dimension you added and what it stands for before writing the recurrence.
Interval DP with an extra state: memoize with the extra dimension, not just (l, r).
Reconstruction: keep a parent pointer or walk the table backwards, never recompute.

calibration: SDE2 bar: climbing stairs, house robber, coin change, LIS, LCS, edit distance, unique paths, word break — define state and transition out loud, then code it, with the space optimization when asked.
SDE3 bar: knapsack variants and the loop-order rules, interval dp (burst balloons), bitmask dp, stock state machines, regex/wildcard matching, and converting memo to table without prompting.

Staff bar (for context): digit dp, dp + data structure optimizations (deque, binary search, segment tree), proving a greedy fails and DP is needed, and estimating state-space size to choose between memo and bottom-up.
Staff bar: explain the extra state and prove the transition is exhaustive; reconstruct the answer, not only its value.
